An Interactive Study

The Seven Levels of Moral Development

Why do you do what's right? The same act — even something as small as brushing your teeth — can spring from seven very different motives. Discover where you tend to reason from, and why each level struggles to see the others.

← Knowledge Centre · Framework by Timothy R. Jennings, MD — Come and Reason Ministries

🪥 The toothbrush test ✍️ Find your level 📖 The seven levels 🔭 Why levels can't see each other

Start here: why does a child brush their teeth? 🪥

Dr. Jennings uses a wonderfully ordinary picture. Picture the same child brushing their teeth — the action is identical every time. But why they do it can climb through all seven levels. Tap each rung to hear the child's reason.

Notice the pattern: fear and bribery at the bottom, then the crowd, then the rule, then love for others, then understanding reality itself, and finally a settled friendship with the Designer where doing right is simply who you are. Same toothbrush. Seven different hearts.

📖 The seven levels, one by one

Each level answers "why do right?" a little more maturely than the last. For each you'll find the toothbrush version, the deeper motive, the view of God and the cross it tends to produce, a Scripture that fits, and questions to sit with.

🔭 Why you can't easily see the other levels

Here's the sobering part. From wherever you stand, the levels below look obvious and childish, and the levels above look naïve, reckless, or even sinful. You literally interpret higher reasoning through your own lens — which is exactly why the Pharisees (Level 4) watched Jesus heal on the Sabbath (Levels 6–7) and concluded He was a lawbreaker. Choose where you stand, then look at another level through your eyes.
